PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers were reported, but the achievement of complete remissions indicates DNA synthesis inhibition and DNA-damage-induced apoptosis pathways were likely activated. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint was met with a 44% overall CR rate, which is clinically meaningful in relapsed/refractory AML. The effect was seen across risk groups and salvage settings. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Subgroup analysis showed differential responses: first salvage patients had higher CR rates (32%) compared to second salvage (10%), and intermediate risk patients (20%) responded better than favorable risk (6%) or unfavorable risk (18%). 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a single-arm Phase I/II study without a control group, but the CR rate substantially exceeds historical expectations for this population. Safety was manageable with pulmonary toxicity being the most common SAE (46%).
